data.title: Week ahead: Barclays, Meta and Netflix results due
data.description:
Monday will bring full-year results from ITM Power, while on the macro calendar, Chinese third-quarter GDP figures and retail sales and industrial production data for September are due.

On Tuesday, investors will eye a third-quarter production report from Anglo American and Q3 trading statements from Bunzl, XP Power and Sabre Insurance. In the US, quarterly results from GE Aerospace and Netflix are due.

On the macro front, the latest UK jobs data will be among the highlights, along with eurozone construction output figures for August and US pending home sales data for September.

On Wednesday, trading updates from Aberdeen, Halfords, Quilter, Segro and Liontrust Asset Management will be in focus, along with Q3 production reports from precious metals miners Fresnillo and Hochschild,

In the US, third-quarter results from Tesla, Meta, Texas Instruments and Philip Morris are due.

Market participants will also turn their attention to UK consumer and producer price inflation data for September.

Thursday will be jam-packed with corporate news. Barclays will release Q3 results, while Sainsbury’s will publish interim results and IG Group is due to put out a strategy update. Q3 trading updates from Inchcape, Rentokil, LSEG, InterContinental Hotels Group and Rathbones will also be eyed, along with nine-month trading updates from Pearson and Relx, and a Q1 trading update from Renishaw.

As far as Sainsbury’s is concerned, AJ Bell analysts Russ Mould and Danni Hewson said: “Mergers and acquisitions are likely to overshadow half-year results after recent reports about a possible multi-billion-pound tie-up with rival Morrisons.

“It only seems like yesterday that Sainsbury’s proposed takeover of Asda in 2019 was blocked by the competition regulator, which begs the question of what has changed in UK food retailing to make mega-deals more palatable.

“Fierce competition has kept UK food inflation below levels forecast earlier in the year, but it accelerated in the four weeks to early October, while some industry groups predict food inflation will touch 7% in 2027.

“How long Sainsbury’s can maintain market share gains while making cost savings to offset rising input costs will be key for free cash flow, dividends and share buybacks.”

In the US, quarterly earnings from Procter & Gamble are scheduled for release, along with the latest initial jobless claims.

On Friday, the latest UK GfK consumer confidence index will be out, while across the pond, American Express is slated to report quarterly earnings.

data.title: Elon Musk may have just taken a major step toward consolidating his empire
data.description:
By William Gavin

Tesla's newly unveiled flying sports car, which features SpaceX rocket thrusters, could help Musk push for a merger between his two biggest companies, analysts say

Tesla on Thursday showed its new Roadster sports car using cold-gas thrusters to jump over the rest of the carmaker's fleet of electric-vehicles, including its Semi and Cybertruck.

A new flying sports car may be exactly what CEO Elon Musk needs to sell Wall Street on a merger between Tesla and SpaceX.

The electric-vehicle maker (TSLA) on Thursday reintroduced the Roadster 2.0, a pricy car that the company showed was capable of hovering in air with the aid of cold-air thrusters designed by SpaceX (SPCX). The event was nine years in the making, but it appears to have paid off.

CFRA analyst Garrett Nelson said the "riveting" unveiling helped convince him to flip to a positive stance on Tesla's stock. He raised his price target to $475 a share from $385 a share, with the new target implying room for the stock to rise 30% from current levels.

"With perception that the 'Musk Magic' is back after a string of uninspiring events and with sentiment at an inflection point, we see little standing in the way of the consummation of a merger to create 'Elon Inc.,' which we think has long been part of Musk's master plan," Nelson wrote in a note to clients on Friday.

Musk is the CEO of both companies, and he's a major shareholder of each as well. During Thursday's event, Musk called the Roadster the "culmination" of a close collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX engineers.

While Wall Street is divided on when Musk will actually push to combine the crown jewels of his empire, Nelson thinks there's a 90% chance it happens by the end of next year. It would be Musk's second major combination of his companies in as many years, after SpaceX acquired xAI in February.

Dan Levy, an analyst at Barclays, expects a merger announcement before Tesla's annual general meeting, which he said has to happen by early December. While a merger could be pitched with a focus on artificial intelligence, given the companies' work on that front, "control is increasingly what may motivate Musk" to pursue a combination, he said in a note to clients on Wednesday.

Representatives for Tesla and SpaceX did not immediately return requests for comment. When asked about a merger during a recent earnings call, Musk told investors that there was "more and more overlap" between the companies, but that he couldn't discuss a combination on that call.

Tesla shares were up by about 1% in recent trading on Friday, while SpaceX's stock was down 1%.

The Roadster was first unveiled by Musk in late 2017, but Tesla repeatedly pushed back planned demonstrations of its progress. On Thursday, Musk said it would go into production in 2028, whereas the initial target was for 2020.

It's still unclear when Tesla aims to begin delivering the car to customers, or even how much it will cost. Tesla is currently taking $50,000 reservations for a "Performance" version of the Roadster, which would come without the SpaceX thrusters.

In 2017, Tesla said it would sell 1,000 "Founders Series" models, each of which required buyers to put down $250,000 at the time. At least one of those customers said his reservation was converted into an order for a Roadster capable of using SpaceX thrusters to reach high speeds. Buying a Roadster that can actually hover in the air requires an invitation from Tesla, according to its website.

"Musk is blending the future of mobility together by integrating auto and rocket technology; at the very least it's a subtle plant in investors' minds making an engineering efficiency argument for a merger," Bill Birmingham, head of research at exchange-traded-product provider Rex Financial, told MarketWatch over email.

-William Gavin

data.title: REG - Thames Wtr Util. Ltd - Recapitalisation Update - Class B Creditors
data.description:
RNS Number : 3856Z Thames Water Utilities Limited 16 October 2026  

Thames Water Utilities Limited

16 October 2026

Recapitalisation Update - Agreement Reached with Class B Creditors

Thames Water Utilities Limited (the "Company" or "Thames Water") announces that it has entered into a transaction support agreement (the "Class B TSA") with certain Class A creditors (the "Consenting Class A Creditors") and certain Class B creditors (the "Consenting Class B Creditors"), including an ad hoc group of Class B Creditors (the "Class B AHG").

Thames Water, the London & Valley Water consortium ("L&VW"), Ofwat and other regulators have been engaged in constructive discussions regarding the proposed recapitalisation of Thames Water for the benefit of customers, employees and the environment. These discussions remain ongoing and, at this stage, the Company's Board, Ofwat, other regulators and relevant investment committees have made no decision to accept and take forward any proposal from L&VW to implementation.

The Class B TSA includes certain terms for the Class B Creditors' treatment (the "Class B Terms") under any future recapitalisation of the Thames Water group which is supported by Class A creditors and super senior creditors who hold at least 66.66% of the Class A and super senior debt respectively (the "Recapitalisation"), expected to be implemented by way of a restructuring plan ("RP2"). The Class B TSA, which is legally binding on its parties, was entered into on 16 October 2026 by the Company, the Consenting Class A Creditors, and Consenting Class B Creditors who hold in aggregate in excess of 60% of the Class B Debt.

The Class B Terms therefore remain subject to overall agreement of the terms of the Recapitalisation. As engagement remains ongoing, there is no certainty that the Recapitalisation will be finally agreed or, therefore, that the Class B Terms will ultimately be implemented.

Notwithstanding the progress that has been made on the terms and structuring of the Recapitalisation, the Company does not currently have sufficient certainty that RP2 can be implemented before certain senior debt matures and the stable platform period expires in March 2027. The stable platform period was introduced following the Thames Water group's interim restructuring transaction in 2025 (the "Interim Platform Transaction") to provide enough time to agree and implement the Recapitalisation. The Company's parent, Thames Water Utilities Holdings Limited ("TWUHL"), therefore intends to implement a further interim transaction to extend the maturities of certain senior debt instruments and the stable platform period (the "SPP Extension Transaction"). The Company is in constructive discussions with its stakeholders about the SPP Extension Transaction.

The Company remains focused on securing a market-led solution which delivers improvements for customers and the environment as soon as practicable.

Highlights of the Class B Terms

The current terms of the Recapitalisation continue to contemplate a write-off in full of the Class B Debt.

The Class B Terms provide that in exchange for the write-off of the full c.£1 billion of Class B Debt, Class B Creditors will receive:

·    post restructured equity in the Thames Water group of a percentage which gives the Class B creditors a recovery of c.5.9%;

·    the right to participate in £150 million of any new equity contemplated by the Recapitalisation[1]; and

·    5.9% participation rights in respect of certain additional tiers of new debt or preferred equity which is included in the terms of the Recapitalisation.

The Class B Terms also provide for payment of certain costs incurred through to implementation of the Recapitalisation; consent fees and a work fee for certain Consenting Class B Creditors to be paid upon implementation of any Recapitalisation. The Company intends to continue servicing interest payments on Class A and Class B debt in full in cash up to the completion date of any Recapitalisation.

No fees or costs will be payable by the Company pursuant to the Class B TSA unless and until the Recapitalisation happens. Any such fees or costs will be funded from the proceeds of the Recapitalisation and not met using customer funds. The Consenting Class B Creditors have agreed to support both the SPP Extension Transaction and the Recapitalisation subject to (i) the Class B Terms being included in any Recapitalisation which is proposed by the Thames Water group; and (ii) Ofwat having launched a public consultation in relation to the Recapitalisation on or before 30 December 2027. The Class B TSA does not impose any obligation on the Company or the Thames Water group to propose a Recapitalisation (whether on any terms proposed by L&VW or otherwise) - the terms of the Recapitalisation (other than the treatment of the Class B Creditors, as set out above) continue to be discussed between the Company and its relevant stakeholders.

Class B Creditors are encouraged to accede to the Class B TSA. Class B Creditors can contact the Company with questions on how to accede to the Class B TSA.

Discussions with the Company's remaining financial stakeholders in relation to the terms of the Recapitalisation are expected to continue.

data.title: Apple faces risk to dominance in UK tap-to-pay market - report
data.description:
Apple is said to be preparing for a legal fight with a U.K. regulator with a view to protect its dominance in the country's tap-to-pay market, the Financial Times reported.

The U.K. Competition and Markets Authority is set to publish proposals for a consultation next week, which is related to making the iPhone maker open up its digital wallet technology to rival payment providers, several people familiar with the matter told the FT.

The consultation is expected to argue on whether Apple exercises unfair power over the U.K.'s tap-to-pay market and recommend changes to the iPhone's operating system, the sources reportedly said.

Apple is likely to legally challenge the decision, two people briefed on the matter told the newspaper.

The regulatory action, if successful, could be a coup for fintechs such as PayPal , Revolut , and Monzo, as well as traditional banks, the report published on Friday noted.

(16:42 GMT) DHL Group Lifts Guidance After Positive Earnings, Strong Peak-Season Forecast

By Andrea Figueras

DHL Group upgraded its outlook for 2026 on the back of positive momentum and prospects of a strong seasonal peak in the last quarter of the year.

The German logistics company said Friday that it now expects earnings before interest and taxes to surpass 7 billion euros, or $7.86 billion, compared with a prior forecast of more than 6.5 billion euros. The group intends to review its midterm earnings guidance in March.

"Business development in the third quarter showed a broad-based growth in demand and, overall, positive earnings momentum for the group, particularly in the DHL Express division," it said.

According to preliminary figures, the group made EBIT of roughly 1.71 billion euros for the quarter through September, up around 16% compared with the same period a year earlier. Group revenue jumped more than 12% on year to nearly 22.6 billion euros.

The company also upgraded its target for free cash flow excluding net mergers and acquisitions to more than 3.2 billion euros, up from approximately 3 billion euros previously.

Capital expenditure is now estimated at around 3.6 billion euros from a prior range between 3 billion euros and 3.3 billion euros.

DHL plans to publish its third-quarter report on Nov. 5.

data.title: Chile's pension funds requested curbs on interest-rate bets before losses, Bloomberg reports
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chile pension funds hit by interest-rate-related positions
  • Losses have drawn criticism from lawmakers, pensioners
  • Congress approved key pension reform in 2025, with the rollout beginning in stages

Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

The report said that fund managers had flagged risks of positions that have since hit the system's most conservative fund hard. The losses have drawn criticism from some lawmakers and raised concerns among pensioners.

Chile's private pension system is managed by firms known as Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFPs), or pension fund administrators, which oversee five investment funds ranging from Fund A, the riskiest, to Fund E, the most conservative.

Earlier this week, the AFP Association's head of research, Roberto Fuentes Silva, attributed a decline in Fund E to rising US interest rates after Bloomberg reported that Chilean pension funds had posted losses of about $7.7 billion on interest-rate-related positions.

Executives managing these pension funds had asked regulators in private conversations to enforce rules on the stockpiling of volatile derivatives, Bloomberg's Thursday report said, citing people familiar with the conversations.

The lucrative nature of the trade meant the executives could not act independently without forgoing returns that rivals would continue to cash in, the report added.

Chile's pension regulator did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Chilean lawmaker Nelson Venegas from the opposition Socialist Party described the AFP losses as "very serious," accusing pension fund managers of putting workers' savings at risk and calling for tougher measures against those responsible.

Ximena Ossandón, a lawmaker from the right-leaning National Renewal party aligned with the government, said it was too early to draw conclusions and that authorities should first determine whether the AFPs had acted within existing regulations.

“We should wait to determine whether the investments were made within the permitted framework or not," Ossandón said in a statement.

The AFP Association has sought to reassure contributors, saying in a statement that pension fund performance should be assessed over the long term rather than based on short-term market fluctuations.

"A pension fund does not have losses or gains; rather, it experiences increases or decreases in its valuation," Fuentes Silva told local media.

Chile's current private pension system started in the early 1980s during the Augusto Pinochet dictatorship and relies solely on worker contributions managed by the AFPs.

The system has long faced criticism for generating relatively low pensions while AFP operators continue to post significant profits. After years of political debate, Congress approved a major pension reform in January 2025, with the rollout beginning in stages from August last year and continuing over several years.

data.title: Tech Stocks Slump as Nasdaq Faces Weekly Loss — WSJ
data.description:
By Chelsey Dulaney

Tech stocks are poised to finish a tough week on a down note as chip and AI-related shares come under new pressure.

The Nasdaq composite is down 1% in midday trading, which would leave the tech-heavy benchmark with a loss of more than 3% for the week. The S&P 500 is down about 0.3% Friday, while the Dow industrials are lower by 0.2% but still up for the week.

The AI trade remains on fragile footing, with CoreWeave shares coming under renewed pressure today. The Nvidia-backed compute provider has been at the center of this week's tech rout, as investors fret over how higher borrowing costs will hit the most highly-leveraged players in the data-center buildout.

Markets had been steadying earlier, while investors pared bets that the Fed will raise interest rates this month after comments from Chairman Kevin Warsh.

Speaking overnight in Bangkok, Warsh did little to dispel investors' view that the Fed isn't in a rush to raise rates despite a string of hotter-than-expected inflation readings this week.

The dollar retreated along with rate-hike expectations. Benchmark 10-year Treasurys are flirting with their best week since February

Brent crude prices are hovering around $105 a barrel.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Brazil's Central Bank Expected to Keep Cutting — Market Talk
data.description: Weaker activity will likely give Brazil's central bank room to keep cutting its hefty interest rates, TS Lombard's João Pedro Oliveira Fachetti says in a note. He expects the BCB to shave a quarter of a percentage point on November 4 and another in December, bringing the Selic rate to 13.25% by year end, while "further cuts hinge on the approval of structural reforms." President Lula da Silva faces right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in the final round of vote on October 25 in a tight race. Bolsonaro is seen as a fiscal hawk and Fachetti says his eventual victory could strengthen the Brazilian real, helping contain inflationary pressures. The real climbs 0.3% against the dollar. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

data.title: SIMCA enters airport advertising market with Rs.5 lakh monthly Shirdi deal
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- SIMCA Advertising Limited has entered the airport advertising segment after securing advertising rights at Shirdi Airport in Maharashtra from Maharashtra Airport Development Company Limited (MADC), with the contract carrying an estimated consideration of Rs.5 lakh per month, plus applicable taxes.

In a regulatory filing to the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) on October 15, the company said it had secured the advertising rights on a leave and licence basis on the city side of Shirdi Airport, located in the Kakdi region of Maharashtra.

The agreement is expected to run for an initial period of 24 months from the date of execution and may be extended up to 36 months at MADC's discretion.

However, SIMCA Advertising said the agreement was still being processed and that it would inform the stock exchange once the duly executed agreement was in place.

The Shirdi Airport contract marks SIMCA Advertising's entry into airport media, giving the company an opportunity to expand its out-of-home (OOH) and digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising strategy into transit locations.

OOH advertising includes billboards, hoardings and other promotional displays in public spaces, while DOOH advertising uses digital screens and displays to deliver advertising messages in physical locations.

Airports can offer advertisers access to a diverse audience comprising tourists, business travellers and other passengers. Advertising placements in terminal areas and other high-visibility spaces can provide brands with opportunities to reach travellers during their journeys.

Commenting on the development, Fahim Batliwala, chairman, managing director and promoter of SIMCA Advertising, said the contract marked an important milestone for the company as it entered the airport advertising segment.

"We are delighted to secure advertising rights at Shirdi Airport from Maharashtra Airport Development Company Limited. This marks an important milestone as we enter the airport advertising segment and expand into premium, high-footfall transit locations," Batliwala said.

"Airports offer significant opportunities for brands to connect with diverse audiences through impactful advertising. This expansion into high-value airport media infrastructure strengthens our OOH and DOOH growth strategy," he added.

Shirdi is a prominent religious destination in Maharashtra, attracting pilgrims visiting the Sai Baba temple. The airport advertising rights could give SIMCA access to a location catering to travellers visiting the region.

The company said the upcoming Kumbh Mela could create further opportunities linked to pilgrimage and tourism activity in the region.

data.title: Alcoa rallies after posting higher Q3 profit, seeing strong aluminum fundamentals
data.description:
Alcoa rose 5.8% in Friday's trading after reporting Q3 adjusted earnings that easily beat analyst expectations, helped by higher aluminum production and prices.

Q3 GAAP earnings more than doubled to $483M, or $1.81/share, from $232M, or $0.88/share, in the year-earlier quarter, and revenues rose 24% Y/Y to $3.7B but came in slightly below Wall Street estimates; adjusted EBITDA jumped to $789M from $270M a year ago.

Q3 aluminum production rose 12% Y/Y to 649K metric tons, aluminum shipments increased 13% to 693K tons, and the average realized third-party price for aluminum surged 34% to $4,527/metric ton.

Q3 alumina production edged up 0.6% Y/Y to 2.47M tons, alumina third-party shipments fell 25% to 1.65M tons, and the average realized third-party price for alumina slipped 6.4% Y/Y to $353/ton.

For the full year, Alcoa reiterated its forecasts for aluminum production of 2.4M-2.6M metric tons, aluminum shipments of 2.6M-2.8M tons, alumina production of 9.5M-9.6M tons, and alumina shipments of 11.5M-11.6M tons.

Aluminum prices have moderated from their recent highs, but pricing remains supported by constructive market fundamentals, CEO Bill Oplinger said on the company's earnings conference call.

"On the supply side, production is gradually recovering as Middle East smelters restart and Indonesian capacity ramps up," although the timing of a full recovery to levels preceding pre-war production levels in the Middle East remains uncertain, Oplinger said.

"Global aluminum inventories remain historically low at ~42 days of consumption, leaving the market with limited capacity to absorb further supply disruptions or stronger-than-expected demand," the CEO said.

Alcoa CFO Molly Beerman said the company believes the momentum displayed in the recent quarter will continue through the end of the year.

"We are expecting higher production and shipments in both [the aluminum and alumina] segments as improved refining system stability is maintained and the smelting portfolio continues to deliver productivity through incremental output and cost discipline," Beerman said on the call.

"While we expect some higher direct input costs from elevated market prices and planned maintenance to support continued operational stability, the underlying performance remains very strong headed into the final quarter of the year."

data.title: China Moves to Control AI Tech Exports While Taiwan Cracks Down on Smuggling — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Sabrina Escobar

The competition for AI supremacy is global and accelerating, and on Friday it was on full display in Asia.

China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology published a joint draft document that would restrict or ban exports of 40 technologies, including AI technology, solar power, and biomedicine.

A little over half — 23 — of the items added to the proposed list are tied to large-scale AI models, agents, semiconductors, and computing clusters.

"The Chinese government's necessary management of these technologies aims to solidify the security baseline, prevent misuse and abuse, ensure that AI remains under human control, and promote international governance of AI," a commerce ministry spokesperson said in a statement.

The spokesperson emphasized that "the vast majority of AI technologies will still be freely exportable," including most of China's open-source models.

Technology exports involving open-source AI technologies will have automatic licensing applied, providing a streamlined export process, the spokesperson said, while technologies that have already entered the public domain and any web, app, or software-as-a-service tools based on restricted models will be excluded from the scope of the export controls.

That is an important distinction. Although the U.S. is leading the AI race with better high-end AI models and semiconductor technology, China's cheaper open-source models may give the country an edge when it comes to winning in terms of model adoption. Given American dominance of the semiconductor market, any Chinese chip export controls likely won't make a big dent on the semi industry.

China's commerce and science and technology ministries are now soliciting public opinions on the new exports restrictions, meaning there could be changes to the final list. Until the final draft is approved and enforced, though, exporters are being required to register any activity that falls under the scope of the draft list.

China's attempt to curb access to high-end technology isn't a big surprise, and may just be a response to the U.S.'s own longstanding tech export controls. The U.S. has long cut China off from its cutting-edge AI semiconductors and manufacturing equipment made by companies like Nvidia, but much of it still gets smuggled into China.

The U.S. is enlisting Taiwan, which produces the bulk of the world's semiconductors, to help stem the flow.

Taipei will add AI servers and cutting-edge semiconductors to a list of controlled export items, making it a criminal offense to ship them to China, according to a Bloomberg interview with Taiwan's Minister of Economic Affairs Kung Ming-hsin. Currently, there are few enforceable penalties for shipping unauthorized technology to China.

"Going forward, some of our measures on controlled items will correspond to American ones because we have made quite some commitments in the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade," Kung told Bloomberg, referring to the trade deal that the U.S. and Taiwan signed this year.

The Taiwanese Embassy didn't immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

Write to Sabrina Escobar at sabrina.escobar@barrons.com. Follow her on X and subscribe to her Barron's Global Signals newsletter.

data.title: Trump move to restart direct US flights with Lebanon hits roadblock
data.description:
Key points:
  • UN regulator report finds safety issues at Beirut airport
  • Findings may hamper Trump's plan to resume US-Lebanon flights
  • Lebanon says corrective action being taken, progress delayed by war

By Allison Lampert and David Shepardson

The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights.

Trump made the announcement in July and signed an order last month for the US government to allow direct flights from the US to Lebanon, reversing a four-decade-long suspension after TWA Flight 847 was hijacked and forced to land in Beirut in 1985.

While the US Federal Aviation Administration and the Transportation Security Administration would still need to conduct safety reviews before flights could resume, the Lebanese embassy in Washington called Trump's order "a significant first step toward restoring direct air service between Lebanon and the United States."

However, the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) technical assistance mission to Lebanon in July identified shortcomings at Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport and in the aviation system.

The findings, which two senior industry officials familiar with the matter expect to delay the resumption of service, complicate efforts to follow up on an order Trump signed after meeting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Washington has backed Aoun as it pushes for Iran-backed Hezbollah to be disarmed.

The agency sent its internal report, made at the request of the Lebanese Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA), to Lebanon in September.

AIRPORT LACKS EMERGENCY PLAN: ICAO

Beirut airport's firefighting resources are equipped for single-aisle planes, but not twin-aisle jetliners used for long-haul flights, according to a summary of ICAO's report. The airport also lacks an emergency plan, and its conditional certification has expired, the report said.

"This is a serious and time-critical matter that must be addressed immediately to preserve the airport's operational status," the summary said.

The report also found the Lebanese regulator LCAA lacks qualified inspectors to oversee air traffic control licensing, and has no fully established, operational and independent aircraft accident investigation authority with clearly defined roles.

Such concerns were flagged during a two-day workshop last month where officials from ICAO, Lebanon's government, the FAA and others discussed efforts to revive direct air service, according to the industry officials and an agenda of the meeting seen by Reuters.

Lebanon's Minister of Public Works and Transport Fayez Rasamny said Lebanon was taking steps to address the concerns, with efforts to certify the airport starting on Saturday. The LCAA expects to issue conditional certification in the coming days.

"Most of the issues highlighted in the report had already been identified by the LCAA, and corrective action had already been initiated," Rasamny said in a statement, adding that progress had been delayed by war. Israeli forces remain in southern Lebanon and have continued strikes despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed in June between Israel and Lebanon. Hezbollah, which was not party to the deal, has rejected it.

The FAA and ICAO declined to comment. The US State Department advises Americans not to travel to Lebanon given safety concerns. It said the FAA advises caution for flights operating in Lebanese airspace due to heightened military activity in or around Syria, including the risks of errant long-range surface-to-air missiles originating from Syrian territory.

MIDDLE EAST UNREST DISRUPTS AIR TRAVEL

Foreign airlines have avoided large swathes of Middle East airspace because of missile and drone threats since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February triggered regional hostilities, with an airport in Saudi Arabia the latest site to come under attack.

Lebanon and its national carrier have been praised domestically for maintaining air navigation services and flights, helping to prop up an economy that depends on tourism and remittances.

Three US airline officials told Reuters on the condition of anonymity they do not think any American carriers would resume flights to Lebanon in the near term, citing security concerns.

While there are no direct flights between Beirut and the United States, such service exists between Lebanon and some large European cities.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency said it was aware of the ICAO report and added that EU airlines must conduct their own assessment of an airport's safety and operational readiness before launching services.

data.title: Nymex Overview: U.S. Crude Prices on Track to End Six-Day Streak of Increases — OPIS
data.description:
Crude-oil and refined product futures prices were falling, but most remained on track to post weekly gains.

The November West Texas Intermediate crude contract was down by 45cts to $97.52/bbl in light trade on Friday. The more-active December contract was down 88cts to $95.62/bbl. The front-month contract is currently nearly $6/bbl above last Friday's settlement.

December Brent crude was down by 18cts to $105.74/bbl while January prices were flat at $103.17/bbl. December prices are $1/bbl ahead for the week.

ULSD futures were on track for a second day of declines, with the November contract falling by 5.6cts to $4.7896/gal, still about 5cts ahead of last week's settlement. The more-active December contract was down by 4.37cts to $4.6108/gal.

Most activity in RBOB was also focused on the next-month contract, with November prices falling by 4.08cts to $3.1394/gal and December prices trading 2.7cts lower to $3.0528/gal. RBOB futures are on track to end the week about 15cts/gal lower than last Friday.

U.S. crude prices have seen a six-day streak of increases as supply concerns have supported the market. Friday's declines come even after the Energy Information Administration on Thursday reported a sharp 8.6 million-bbl drop in U.S. commercial crude inventories.

But those concerns are being mitigated by the announcement by the International Energy Agency that member countries have agreed to accelerate the release of 100 million bbls of crude oil and refined products that they had previously announced would be put into markets.

The release is expected to include about 20 million bbl of diesel.

The week's increase in diesel futures prices is being felt by consumers, with the average retail diesel price Friday of $6.3261/gal marking the fourth day of increases and an increase of about 5cts/gal from last Friday.

Gasoline prices around the country Friday averaged $4.3271/gal, about 6cts/gal lower than a week ago.

data.title: Tesla, SpaceX, CoreWeave, Lam Research, Netflix, Strategy, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
Bond Yields Tick Higher After Treasury Doesn't Signal Cuts to Auction Sizes — WSJ
data.description:
By Sam Goldfarb

Longer-term Treasury yields ticked higher after the Treasury department passed on an opportunity to send a strong signal that it is considering reducing the sizes of bond auctions.

In survey ahead of its quarterly refunding announcement on Nov. 4, the agency asked bond dealers for their thoughts on what future changes to auction sizes it should consider "given expected borrowing needs and investor demand." But it didn't say anything more explicit that might have hinted that cuts to longer-term debt auctions were imminent-a signal that some investors had thought was possible given the Trump administration's efforts to push down bond yields.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Crypto.com, Gemini, and a16z among donors in $210.5M flow to Trump super PACs
data.description:
Companies that watched federal enforcement cases against them disappear have since sent serious money to President Trump's political operation. A Public Citizen report published on October 8, 2026 puts the figure at $210.5 million contributed or pledged to pro-Trump super PACs.

Some of crypto's best-known names sit on that donor list. Crypto.com, Gemini, and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz all appear prominently, and the timing of their checks is drawing attention.

The consumer watchdog reviewed the Trump administration's rollback of federal enforcement. It counted 212 enforcement actions that were canceled or weakened, involving 205 corporations.

Public Citizen then cross-referenced those companies against political giving. Collectively, the corporations that benefited have contributed or pledged $210.5 million to groups such as MAGA Inc. and Keep America Great.

Crypto.com stands out. According to the report, the exchange gave $35 million to MAGA Inc. and $2 million to Keep America Great. Those donations followed the SEC's decision to cancel an investigation into the platform over unregistered securities trading.

Gemini's contributions came from both the company and its founders. The exchange donated $20 million to MAGA Inc., while co-founders Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss each personally gave $10 million, bringing the Gemini-linked total to $40 million. Those contributions followed a dropped SEC probe of its own.

Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital firm often called a16z, also made the list. The firm and co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz donated $12 million to MAGA Inc.

The a16z connection runs a little differently. Rather than the firm itself facing a dropped case, Public Citizen found that nine companies in its investment portfolio benefited from the canceled federal actions.

It is worth being precise about what the report documents. It shows a sequence: enforcement was dropped or softened, and donations followed. Public Citizen frames this as a troubling pattern of regulatory relief tied to political giving and raises ethical concerns about corporate money in politics.

The report documents timing and amounts. It does not, based on the findings described, present proof of an explicit exchange of donations for dropped cases.

Gemini's donations came partly from its founders' personal accounts, while Crypto.com's came from the corporate side. a16z's contribution mixed firm and founder money and connects to a wider portfolio of companies.

For investors, the practical question is how much regulatory risk is truly gone versus simply paused. Public Citizen's count of 212 canceled or weakened actions across 205 corporations is a measure of how much changed. It is also a measure of how much could change back.

data.title: Shoppers Stop Swings To Rs 3.11 Cr Profit In Q2 FY27
data.description:
Revenue from operations rose 8.72 per cent to Rs 1,366.27 crore, while the retailer attributed its return to profitability to its premiumisation strategy

Retail chain Shoppers Stop reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 3.11 crore in the September quarter of FY27, reversing a net loss of Rs 20.11 crore in the year-ago period, as its premiumisation strategy supported profitability despite a shift in the festive season towards the December quarter.

Revenue from operations rose 8.72 per cent to Rs 1,366.27 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,256.62 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to the company’s regulatory filing. The Raheja family-promoted retailer attributed its return to profitability to its “premiumisation-led growth strategy”, which it said had enabled a “PAT positive performance”.

Total income, including other income, increased 9.7 per cent to Rs 1,389.15 crore during the quarter. Total expenses rose 7.11 per cent to Rs 1,385.02 crore. Shoppers Stop Managing Director and CEO Kavindra Mishra said the company delivered a strong performance in the second quarter despite the festive season shifting largely to the third quarter this year.

"Our continued focus on premiumisation, experiential retail, inventory discipline and operational excellence is resonating well with customers and strengthening the quality of growth. We remain committed to prudent capital allocation, further improving profitability, and achieving our goal of becoming debt-free by the end of Q3," he said.

Shoppers Stop operates 119 department stores, 12 premium home concept stores, 73 speciality beauty stores featuring brands such as M.A.C, Estee Lauder, Bobbi Brown, Clinique, Jo Malone, NARS, ARMANI beauty and PRADA BEAUTY, alongside its in-house SS Beauty brand. The retailer also runs 82 Intune stores and three airport outlets. Its retail network spans 4.6 million square feet across 75 cities.

data.title: Tata Chemicals Gets Relief As Tribunal Rejects Rs 908 Cr Allied Silica Claim
data.description:
A three-member tribunal unanimously rejected the claim by Allied Silica and promoter Manmohan Singh Jain, but a majority directed Tata Chemicals to pay Rs 1 crore plus interest and certain costs.

Tata Chemicals said on Friday that an arbitration tribunal has unanimously rejected a Rs 908-crore claim filed against it by Allied Silica Limited and its promoter Manmohan Singh Jain, although a majority of the panel directed the company to pay Rs 1 crore, along with interest and certain costs.

The three-member tribunal of the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA) issued its final award on October 15, 2026, the company said in a regulatory filing.

While all three members rejected the claim of Rs 908 crore, a majority of the tribunal directed Tata Chemicals to pay Allied Silica a principal amount of Rs 1 crore, together with interest and certain costs. The dissenting member opposed the payment direction, including the principal amount, interest and costs.

Tata Chemicals said it was examining the final award and would assess its future course of action.

The company had informed stock exchanges on December 11, 2024, that Allied Silica and Jain had initiated arbitration proceedings against it under MCIA rules, seeking Rs 908 crore.

The latest disclosure was made under Regulations 30 and 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

data.title: FSSAI Issues Notices To Gemini Edibles, BigBasket, Flipkart Over Rice Bran Oil Claims
data.description:
FSSAI flagged cholesterol and heart-health claims made for Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018, and raised a separate ecommerce licensing concern involving Gemini Edibles

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued notices to Gemini Edibles & Fats India, BigBasket and Flipkart over allegedly impermissible cholesterol and heart-health claims made in the promotion of Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil. The regulator has also flagged a potential licensing violation by Gemini Edibles over the sale of food products through its own ecommerce website.

In a social media post on Friday, FSSAI said it had issued notices to Hyderabad-based Gemini Edibles and Fats India, Innovative Retail Concepts, which operates BigBasket, and Flipkart India over promotional material for the rice bran oil. The claims included 'Reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol' and references to 10,000 PPM Natural Oryzanol.

"The cholesterol and heart-health claims were found to be not covered/permitted under the applicable claims for edible vegetable oil (rice bran oil) under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018," FSSAI said.

The regulator has asked the three companies to explain why action should not be initiated against them under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The notices concern the alleged violations, and no final penalties against the companies have been announced in connection with the claims.

Separately, FSSAI said Gemini Edibles and Fats India was found offering or selling food products through its own ecommerce website without appearing to hold a valid central licence covering e-commerce activity.

In other enforcement actions, FSSAI suspended the licence of DNV Food Products Ltd after an inspection found serious non-compliances relating to hygiene, sanitation, storage and licensing. The regulator also cancelled the licence of Jhanvittanni over continued non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations.
